Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning briefing.

Let's start with the macro picture. US equity futures are rallying to kick off the week — S&P is up 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Asia was broadly higher overnight, led by Korea up 1.65% and Hong Kong up over 1%. Europe is also in the green, up 85 to 120 basis points, with data center pick-and-shovel names outperforming there. Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. Brent crude is actually sliding 170 basis points to around $102 a barrel. The rally this morning is a little confounding because almost all of the weekend news flow was net negative. What's driving stocks higher is one thing: diplomatic optimism around the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week. Trump reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night and said he'd be open to meeting with Iran's president, who is expected to attend the General Assembly. Markets are essentially betting that even a tiny improvement in Middle East tensions could send oil sharply lower, and that would unleash a cascade of bullish macro effects — lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, reduced margin pressure, and improved consumer confidence. That's the bull thesis in one sentence.

Now let's talk about the bear case, because the weekend headlines were genuinely ugly. The Houthis dramatically escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia, hitting oil infrastructure near Moscow. Iran warned of a fierce response to any resumed US military action. And on the AI side, multiple negative headlines hit after Friday's close: Anthropic's IPO has been delayed, its 2027 revenue projections disappointed investors, OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of approximately $280 billion between 2026 and 2030, and Oracle is facing serious pressure in debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center known as Project Jupiter — efforts to offload those loans have, quote, hit a wall. These are meaningful headwinds for AI infrastructure stocks, even as European data center names are holding up this morning.

On individual names: Disney's parks business is outperforming peers thanks to price promotions and package deals, a bullish data point at a time when competitors are seeing traffic headwinds. Novo Nordisk is sliding in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide granular financial targets. Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California over the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, potentially agreeing to divest Comedy Central and preserve CNN's editorial independence, though not all state attorneys general are on board. And London-based neocloud firm Nscale filed its S1 Friday and plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker N-S-C-L.

On rates and the Fed: the market is pricing about 33 basis points of hikes over the Fed's final two meetings this year, with roughly even odds on a move at the October 28th meeting. Fed officials Schmid and Kashkari both made hawkish comments over the weekend, warning that inflation is running hot well beyond just energy prices. Treasury supply is also worth watching — the government plans to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above 24% of marketable debt.

The key catalysts for the week are the United Nations General Assembly running through September 28th, the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday the 24th, and US flash PMIs on Wednesday morning. There is nothing major on today's calendar specifically. The directional call for today is simple: watch for any Iran-related diplomatic headline out of New York. A positive signal sends oil lower and stocks higher. An escalation headline reverses this morning's gains quickly. Stay nimble.
